docs.title: HospitalSim
docs.text:
HospitalSim is an educational hospital operations project with two complementary components: a no-login browser dashboard for synthetic scenarios and a FastAPI service for relational CRUD backed by MySQL.

Open project documentation Local dashboard Local Swagger API

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Follow Getting started to launch the dashboard or full stack.
  2. Use the Dashboard guide to run scenarios and understand the metrics.
  3. Explore API usage to create hospitals, roles, staff, and patients.
  4. Read the Data model for fields and relationships.
  5. See Development for source layout, tests, and documentation builds.

docs.title: What is simulated?
docs.text:
The website models admissions, department-specific bed capacity, waiting queues, care assignments, and discharges. It contains two fictional hospitals and synthetic patients. A seeded engine makes a fresh scenario reproducible. Each hospital has its own browser-saved state.

The backend stores hospitals, patients, staff, and roles using SQLModel and MySQL. It has no bed or queue tables and no simulation runner. Browser demo actions do not modify the database; Swagger requests do. See Architecture.

Educational scope

There is no authentication. This project is intended for trusted local development with synthetic data, not clinical use or storage of real patient information.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
HospitalSim has a browser simulation and a separate database-backed API. They share a hospital domain, but they do not synchronize records.

Component Technology Responsibility Data lifetime Dashboard React, TypeScript, Vite Views, controls, synthetic scenarios Browser local storage Simulation engine Pure TypeScript functions Seeded arrivals, bed allocation, queues, discharges Part of dashboard state Static server Nginx Serve the built dashboard and SPA fallback Built files API FastAPI, SQLModel Validation and CRUD for four resources MySQL records Database MySQL 8.4 in Compose Relational persistence and foreign keys Named Docker volume Documentation MkDocs Material Guides and data/API reference Markdown source and GitHub Pages

docs.title: Browser path
docs.text:
src/App.tsx manages navigation, forms, an interval timer, and local storage. It calls pure functions in src/simulation.ts, which return new state without mutating their input. A seeded generator supplies repeatable fixtures and random arrivals. CSS and inline SVG draw the interface and chart without external image or font services.

The frontend Docker image runs an npm build in a Node 24 stage, then copies dist/ into Nginx. No Python or database connection is needed to use the dashboard. VITE_SWAGGER_URL is embedded at build time and used only as a navigation link.

docs.title: API path
docs.text:
Each router receives a SQLModel session through get_session, queries or modifies model instances, commits changes, and returns a declared response model. Hospitals, staff, and patients are related through foreign keys; staff and roles are joined through staff_roles.

The FastAPI lifespan function calls SQLModel.metadata.create_all on startup. The engine is created from the required DATABASE_URL environment variable. Compose waits for the database healthcheck before starting the API; /health itself reports process health only.

There is no /api prefix, authentication, authorization, CORS middleware, pagination, or migration framework. Swagger is supplied by FastAPI at /docs. Cross-origin browser API integration would require additional configuration, error handling, and deliberate mapping between the simulation domain and persisted entities.

docs.title: Boundaries to preserve when extending
docs.text:
• Keep demo records synthetic and clearly labeled.
  • Add explicit migrations rather than relying on create_all to alter tables.
  • Define transactional admission and discharge behavior before adding backend bed/queue models.
  • Enforce cross-hospital assignment rules on all affected update paths, not only patient creation.
  • Add authentication and authorization before exposing sensitive records.
  • Add MySQL integration tests for referential actions, conflict handling, and concurrency.

docs.title: Dashboard and simulation
docs.text: The English dashboard opens directly without authentication. Its Overview, Patients, Staff & roles, and Hospitals pages share a hospital selector and simulation toolbar. Documentation and Swagger links remain in the top header.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text:
1. Start on Riverside Medical Center's overview at Day 1, 08:00.
  2. Choose Normal operations and select Run simulation. Watch counts, department capacity, the chart, and activity update.
  3. Select Patient surge or Critical demand, then use +1 hour to see pressure build.
  4. Open Patients. Search by name, ID, department, or clinician and filter by status.
  5. Select Admit patient, enter a synthetic name and age (0–120), and choose a department. The patient receives its department's lead clinician.
  6. Discharge an in-care patient to free a bed. A waiting patient from the same department takes it automatically.
  7. Inspect the care team or select the other hospital. Switching hospitals pauses the simulation and preserves both hospitals' progress.
  8. Use Reset simulation and confirm to restore only the selected hospital.

docs.title: Clock and demand
docs.text:
The clock starts at Day 1, 08:00. One engine step is 15 simulated minutes. At 1×, the timer steps every three real seconds; 2× every 1.5 seconds; 4× every 0.75 seconds. Browser timer throttling can slow background tabs. No offline time is simulated, and a page reload starts paused. +1 hour immediately performs four steps using the selected scenario; it does not change the running/paused setting.

Preset Arrivals per step What changes Normal operations 1–3 Lower incoming demand Patient surge 4–6 Higher incoming demand Critical demand 7–9 Highest incoming demand

Scenario choice changes arrival counts only. It does not change severity, mortality, staffing, or care quality. Random choices come from a deterministic seeded generator; a fresh reset with the same sequence of actions produces the same results.

docs.title: Capacity and care
docs.text:
Hospital Emergency General medicine Intensive care Surgery Total beds Staff Riverside Medical Center 18 32 10 20 80 24 Northview Community Hospital 12 24 6 14 56 16

Riverside starts with 54 in-care patients; Northview starts with 38. Departments are chosen uniformly for generated arrivals, so a department may be full even when beds remain elsewhere. Patients wait for their chosen department; the model does not transfer them between departments.

Generated patients are 18–87 years old. New patients have a stay of 60–479 simulated minutes, checked at each 15-minute step. The baseline patients have varied remaining stays. A queued patient's care clock starts when a bed becomes available. Each step discharges eligible patients, promotes waiting patients in their arrival order within the department, and generates new arrivals. Manual discharges also promote the queue immediately.

Eight named clinicians represent care teams. Only the four lead clinicians receive automated patient assignments; nurses are shown as part of the representative roster. Total staff counts are fixed scenario inputs and do not constrain bed assignments. Roles are descriptive, not access permissions.

docs.title: Metric definitions
docs.text:
Metric Definition Active patients In-care patients plus waiting patients Bed occupancy In-care patients divided by total beds, rounded to a whole percentage Staff on duty Fixed hospital fixture: 24 or 16 Waiting for care Patients queued because their department has no free bed Admissions New generated and manually admitted patients since reset; excludes baseline patients Discharges Completed and manually discharged patients since reset; includes baseline patients who leave Department capacity In-care count divided by department beds; amber at 90% or more Assigned patients In-care patients currently assigned to that named clinician

The chart plots cumulative admissions and discharges using at most 25 samples. During uninterrupted stepping, this spans the latest six simulated hours; labels show simulation clock time. The activity feed retains the latest 40 events, with four shown on Overview. The directory retains all active records and up to 200 discharged records after each step. Totals remain cumulative even when older history is removed.

docs.title: Persistence and reset
docs.text:
State is saved in local storage under hospitalsim.demo.v1 for the current browser origin. Only simulation state is persisted; navigation, speed, hospital selection, and preset return to their defaults on refresh. Separate ports, browsers, devices, or private browsing sessions have independent state.

If storage is blocked or full, an on-screen notice explains that progress may not survive a refresh, but the simulation continues in memory. Resetting a hospital is confirmed in a dialog and leaves the other hospital intact. Clear site data to remove all browser demo progress.

docs.title: Data boundary
docs.text: This dashboard makes no API data requests. The patient ages, departments, status, stay lengths, bed counts, and chart data are frontend simulation fields. They are not a representation of the backend's persisted schema. Opening Swagger lets you work with independent MySQL-backed CRUD records.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Responsibility app/main.py FastAPI setup, router registration, startup table creation, health route app/database.py SQLModel engine, environment configuration, per-request session app/models/ Table models and request/response schemas app/routers/ CRUD and relationship checks web/src/App.tsx Dashboard views, forms, timer, and persistence web/src/simulation.ts Pure seeded simulation engine web/src/App.css / index.css Dashboard layout, styling, and responsive rules web/tests/ Node-based simulation tests tests/ Isolated SQLite API regression tests docs/ / mkdocs.yml Documentation source and navigation compose.yml API, frontend, and MySQL services

docs.title: Frontend checks
docs.text:
cd web
npm ci
npm test
npm run build

Tests use Node 24's native TypeScript stripping and built-in test runner, without a separate test dependency. They verify repeatability, immutable transitions, capacity limits, conservation of active patients, first-in queue promotion, demand differences, bounded history, and time rollover. The production build checks TypeScript before Vite bundles the app. npm run lint is available for Oxlint checks.

For new simulation behavior, prefer pure engine functions and tests for meaningful constraints. For UI work, check keyboard navigation, modal focus, narrow screens, empty search results, waiting queues, state persistence, and unavailable browser storage. These engine tests do not execute browser interactions.

docs.title: Python dependencies
docs.text:
uv sync --locked

After an intentional backend dependency change:

uv lock
uv export --format requirements-txt --no-dev --no-emit-project --output-file requirements.txt

Commit pyproject.toml, uv.lock, and requirements.txt together. Docker installs the exported requirements; uv development uses the lockfile. PyMySQL includes its RSA extra for MySQL password authentication. The declared Python version is 3.14+.

docs.title: Backend validation
docs.text:
Start an accessible MySQL database, export DATABASE_URL, and run the service. Use Swagger to exercise create/list/read/patch/delete for all four resources, including missing IDs, duplicate names, invalid dates, invalid references, and same-hospital staff assignment. Verify records persist across a service restart. Run the isolated API regression suite with:

uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

These tests override the database session with in-memory SQLite and skip the production lifespan hook, so they do not create or modify production tables. They cover health, Swagger/OpenAPI, the hospital/role/staff/patient relationship chain, all CRUD methods, duplicate hospitals, cross-hospital assignments, and invalid birth dates. Explicit SQLAlchemy relationship targets avoid deferred type annotations being interpreted as ORM class names on Python 3.14. These checks do not constitute a MySQL integration test suite.

The existing API does not fully guard every null PATCH, deletion, or staff transfer case. Add appropriate integrity validation and transaction handling when extending those paths. create_all is not a migration mechanism.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
uv run mkdocs serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8000
uv run mkdocs build --strict

The explicit port avoids conflicting with API development conventions. Markdown sources are English. Navigation is declared in mkdocs.yml; add new pages there. Mermaid diagrams are supported through the configured SuperFences extension.

The GitHub Actions workflow builds and publishes on pushes to main. Configure GitHub Pages to serve gh-pages; the site URL is https://marcelopenas.github.io/HospitalSim/. Local edits or a source archive do not publish a documentation update automatically.

docs.title: Course deliverables
docs.text:
The accompanying SQL brief asks for FastAPI, ORM/MySQL persistence, CRUD for at least two entities, multiple data types, and a well-documented repository. The project implements CRUD for hospitals, staff, roles, and patients. Patient dates, integer IDs, and text fields demonstrate varied types.

Before submission, the owner should verify repository access for the instructors, maintain meaningful commits, record the required API demonstration video, add the video's real URL to the README, and review the AI-assistance disclosure. Those external deliverables cannot be inferred from the source archive.

docs.title: Dashboard without a backend
docs.text:
Install Node.js 24 and npm, then run from the repository root:

cd web
npm ci
npm run dev

Open Vite's printed URL, normally http://localhost:5173. No login or database setup is needed. The top Documentation link opens this project's GitHub Pages documentation; Swagger API opens the local backend's /docs page if that service is running.

docs.title: Full stack with Docker
docs.text:
Install Docker and Compose v2. From the repository root:

cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env to review development passwords and other settings.
docker compose up --build

You can also use bash run.sh, which creates .env from the example if absent and runs Compose. It does not delete database volumes. Add -d to start in the background.

Component URL Dashboard http://localhost:3000 Swagger http://localhost:8080/docs ReDoc http://localhost:8080/redoc OpenAPI JSON http://localhost:8080/openapi.json Health http://localhost:8080/health

The database may take a short time to initialize. Compose waits for MySQL to respond before starting the API. SQLModel creates missing tables at API startup. The API database is initially empty; frontend data is seeded independently.

docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f web
docker compose down

docker compose down preserves the db-data volume. To rebuild the web dashboard after changing its source or build variables, run docker compose up --build frontend.

docs.title: Local Python development
docs.text:
The declared minimum is Python 3.14. Install uv, supply an accessible MySQL database and user, then run:

uv sync --locked
export DATABASE_URL='mysql+pymysql://hospitalsim:YOUR_PASSWORD@localhost:3306/hospitalsim'
uv run fastapi dev app/main.py --port 8080

The API does not automatically load .env. Export the connection string in the process environment. The default Compose database has no host port mapping, so local Python cannot reach that database at localhost:3306 unless you explicitly add a mapping. Use a local MySQL server or a Compose override for that development mode.

docs.title: Environment configuration
docs.text:
Variable Meaning DATABASE_URL SQLAlchemy/PyMySQL URL; required when starting Python directly MYSQL_DATABASE Database created by the MySQL container on first initialization MYSQL_USER / MYSQL_PASSWORD Application database user, distinct from root MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD MySQL root initialization password SQL_ECHO true enables SQL logging; defaults to false VITE_SWAGGER_URL Optional public, build-time URL for the top Swagger link

For Docker, root .env supplies Compose interpolation and the frontend build argument. For Vite development, put VITE_SWAGGER_URL in web/.env.local. The default Swagger link uses the browser hostname, HTTP, and port 8080. Set an explicit HTTPS URL when deploying over HTTPS. Never put secrets in VITE_ variables.

Use URL-safe passwords or percent-encode special characters in a database URL. The example credentials are local development defaults. Existing MySQL volumes retain initialized users and passwords even after you edit .env; update database users explicitly when changing credentials.

docs.title: The dashboard works but Swagger does not open
docs.text: The dashboard is self-contained; Swagger needs the API. Start the full stack and check http://localhost:8080/health. The default Swagger URL is http://<browser hostname>:8080/docs. Set VITE_SWAGGER_URL when using an external API or HTTPS, then restart Vite or rebuild the frontend image. Vite variables are build-time values.

docs.title: MySQL connection or authentication fails
docs.text:
Check docker compose ps and docker compose logs web db. Ensure root .env exists with all four MYSQL_ variables. Compose uses the internal hostname db, while a local Python process needs a connection string reachable from the host. The default database container does not publish port 3306.

A MySQL volume retains initialized users and passwords. Editing .env alone does not change existing database users. Update those users deliberately, or use a separate fresh volume for disposable test data. Do not remove a volume containing data you need.

If Python fails with KeyError: DATABASE_URL, export the variable before starting the API. The application does not load .env itself. URL-encode special characters in database connection URLs. Use the supplied locked/exported dependencies, including PyMySQL's RSA extra.

docs.title: Startup fails after a schema change
docs.text: create_all creates missing tables and does not alter existing columns. Apply an explicit database migration when changing an existing schema. Do not expect a rebuild to migrate or clear the database.

docs.title: API records do not appear on the dashboard
docs.text: This is expected: MySQL-backed CRUD and browser simulation are independent. Use Swagger to inspect API records. The website uses its own synthetic fixtures and browser storage.

docs.title: Patients wait even though the hospital has free beds
docs.text: Beds belong to departments. A patient waiting for an intensive-care bed cannot use an empty surgery bed in this model. Discharge an in-care patient from the same department or advance time. Critical demand can create a sustained queue.

docs.title: The clock or chart seems paused
docs.text: Select Run simulation. Reloading the page and switching hospitals pause the timer. An inactive browser tab may throttle timers, and no offline progression is applied. +1 hour advances time immediately. The chart begins without generated arrivals and keeps only its latest 25 samples, while counters stay cumulative.

docs.title: Progress is missing after reopening the page
docs.text: Progress is specific to the current origin (scheme, hostname, and port) and browser. Different localhost ports have different storage. Private browsing or clearing site data can remove it. If storage is blocked or full, the dashboard shows a notice and continues without durable persistence.

docs.title: A request returns 400, 409, 422, or 500
docs.text: Use IDs returned by your server rather than assuming the example IDs. Check relationship prerequisites and the detail response. Names and locations can conflict; patient birth dates must be in the past; staff assigned to a patient must belong to the same hospital. Explicit nulls for required PATCH fields, deletes with dependents, and certain staff transfers can trigger unhandled integrity errors. Inspect server logs and see the API guide.

docs.title: The build fails on an older Node or Python
docs.text: Use Node 24 for the dashboard and its native TypeScript tests, and Python 3.14+ for the backend. Reinstall frontend dependencies with npm ci, and Python dependencies with uv sync --locked. Use npm run build to catch TypeScript errors before packaging.

docs.title: Port 3000, 5173, or 8080 is already in use
docs.text: Change the published Compose port or use Vite's --port option. If the API port changes, update VITE_SWAGGER_URL and rebuild/restart the frontend. For local documentation, use mkdocs serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: API usage
docs.text:
The API is available at http://localhost:8080 in the default Compose setup. There is no /api prefix. Swagger UI, ReDoc, and the OpenAPI schema describe the running service.

Swagger's Try it out sends real requests and changes MySQL records. It does not change the browser simulation.

docs.title: Resources and methods
docs.text:
Replace {id} with the integer resource ID. The actual parameter names are hospital_id, patient_id, staff_id, and role_id.

Resource Collection Item Methods Hospitals /hospitals /hospitals/{id} POST, GET collection; GET, PATCH, DELETE item Roles /roles /roles/{id} POST, GET collection; GET, PATCH, DELETE item Staff /staff /staff/{id} POST, GET collection; GET, PATCH, DELETE item Patients /patients /patients/{id} POST, GET collection; GET, PATCH, DELETE item

All create/update payloads are JSON. Successful creates return the new record with status 201; list/read/update responses use 200; deletes use 204 with no body. PATCH applies supplied fields, rather than replacing the record. Lists return JSON arrays without pagination, search, filters, or an ordering guarantee. There is no PUT endpoint.

docs.title: Create a complete relationship chain
docs.text: Create a hospital and role, then staff, then a patient. Example IDs assume a fresh database; always use IDs actually returned by your API.

docs.title: 1. Hospital
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/hospitals \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Demo Hospital","location":"Boston"}'

{"id":1,"name":"Demo Hospital","location":"Boston"}

docs.title: 2. Role
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/roles \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Physician","description":"Provides patient care"}'

{"id":1,"name":"Physician","description":"Provides patient care"}

docs.title: 3. Staff
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/staff \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"first_name":"Olivia","last_name":"Chen","hospital_id":1,"role_ids":[1]}'

{"id":1,"first_name":"Olivia","last_name":"Chen","hospital_id":1,"role_ids":[1]}

docs.title: 4. Patient
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/patients \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"first_name":"Alex","last_name":"Taylor","date_of_birth":"1990-05-12","hospital_id":1,"staff_id":1}'

{"id":1,"first_name":"Alex","last_name":"Taylor","date_of_birth":"1990-05-12","hospital_id":1,"staff_id":1}

staff_id may be omitted or set to null at patient creation. When supplied, it must identify staff at the patient's hospital. date_of_birth is an ISO date strictly before today's UTC date.

docs.title: Read, update, and delete
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8080/patients
curl http://localhost:8080/patients/1

curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/patients/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"first_name":"Alexandra","staff_id":null}'

curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/staff/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"role_ids":[]}'

curl -i -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/patients/1

staff_id: null explicitly unassigns a patient; omitting it leaves the assignment unchanged. For staff PATCH, role_ids: [] removes all roles, omission or null leaves existing roles unchanged, and a list replaces the set of roles. Duplicate input role IDs collapse to unique relationships.

Delete dependents first: patients, then staff, then hospitals; remove staff-role links by updating/deleting staff before deleting roles. The API does not offer a documented cascade-delete contract or translate every database integrity failure into an HTTP conflict.

docs.title: Validation and errors
docs.text:
Status Typical meaning 400 Missing referenced hospital/staff/role; patient and clinician belong to different hospitals 404 Requested item ID not found 409 Duplicate hospital name/location, or duplicate role name 422 Invalid request schema, empty/overlong string, missing required field, or non-past birth date 500 Unhandled server/database error; check logs

Router errors use an envelope such as:

{"detail":"staff_id and hospital_id must refer to the same hospital"}

FastAPI's 422 response has a structured detail array describing field validation errors. Check the actual response body instead of relying on status alone.

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text: There is no authentication, pagination, filtering, or backend simulation state. Hospital uniqueness is enforced in the database and router; role-name uniqueness is checked only by the router and can race under concurrent requests. Required database fields are typed as optional in PATCH schemas, so explicitly setting them to null can result in an integrity error; send non-null values. Some staff hospital changes and deletion operations are not fully checked against existing patient relationships. Do not assume every invalid relationship operation returns a clean 4xx response.

docs.title: Health endpoint
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8080/health

{"status":"ok"}

This confirms the process responds; it does not execute a database readiness query.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
SQLModel maps Python entities to MySQL tables. Create, read, and update schemas live beside each table model in app/models/. Integer primary keys are generated by the database.

erDiagram
    HOSPITAL ||--o{ STAFF : employs
    HOSPITAL ||--o{ PATIENT : receives
    STAFF o|--o{ PATIENT : treats
    STAFF ||--o{ STAFF_ROLES : has
    ROLE ||--o{ STAFF_ROLES : assigned
Model Table Main fields Relationships Hospital hospital id, name, location Many staff and patients Patient patient id, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, hospital_id, staff_id One hospital; optional staff Staff staff id, first_name, last_name, hospital_id One hospital; many patients and roles Role role id, name, description Many staff through staff_roles StaffRoleLink staff_roles staff_id, role_id Composite primary key and two foreign keys

The API serializes staff roles as a role_ids list rather than embedding Role objects. Relationships are not recursively included in read responses.

Browser departments, beds, queue statuses, and simulated stays are separate frontend concepts, not columns in this schema. See Architecture.

docs.title: Hospital
docs.text:
A hospital is the parent facility for staff and patients. Defined in app/models/hospital.py; managed through /hospitals.

Field Type Required on create Validation id integer Generated Primary key, read-only in API payloads name string Yes 1–200 characters; unique location string Yes 1–500 characters; unique

Location is free text; it is not parsed or verified as a postal address. Name and location each have separate database uniqueness constraints and router-level conflict checks.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: A hospital has many staff and patients. Each of those records references one hospital through hospital_id. Hospital responses contain only id, name, and location, without embedded relationship arrays.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{"name":"Riverside Medical Center","location":"Boston, Massachusetts"}

PATCH may supply either name or location. Omit unchanged fields and do not set required values to null. A missing item returns 404 and a detected duplicate returns 409. Remove dependent staff and patients before deleting a hospital; deletion behavior is not normalized into a complete API-level integrity-error contract.

docs.title: Patient
docs.text:
A patient belongs to one hospital and can optionally be assigned a staff member. Defined in app/models/patient.py; managed through /patients.

Field Type Required on create Validation id integer Generated Primary key first_name string Yes 1–100 characters last_name string Yes 1–100 characters date_of_birth ISO date Yes Strictly before the current UTC date hospital_id integer Yes Must identify an existing hospital staff_id integer or null No If present, existing staff in the same hospital

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "first_name":"Alex",
  "last_name":"Taylor",
  "date_of_birth":"1990-05-12",
  "hospital_id":1,
  "staff_id":1
}

The read schema returns these fields plus the generated id. It does not include medical history, diagnosis, beds, departments, admission status, or treatment records.

docs.title: Updates and relationships
docs.text:
Omit staff_id in PATCH to retain the current assignment; set it to null to unassign. When moving a patient, update hospital_id and provide compatible staff_id in the same request, or unassign the staff member. The router checks the resulting patient/hospital/staff combination on create and update.

A nonexistent referenced hospital or staff member, or a cross-hospital assignment, returns 400. A missing patient returns 404; an invalid birth date returns 422. Required fields should never be explicitly set to null in PATCH.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Roles describe staff occupations or responsibilities. They do not grant authentication or access-control permissions. Defined in app/models/role.py; managed through /roles.

Field Type Required on create Validation id integer Generated Primary key name string Yes 1–100 characters description string or null No At most 500 characters

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{"name":"Physician","description":"Provides clinical care"}

The router rejects duplicate names with 409 when creating or renaming roles. There is no database unique constraint on role.name, so this check alone is not concurrency-safe. Missing role IDs return 404.

docs.title: Staff relationships
docs.text: Staff and roles have a many-to-many relationship through StaffRoleLink, stored in staff_roles with composite primary key (staff_id, role_id). Assign and remove roles through a staff member's role_ids field. Clear related assignments before deleting a role. Role PATCH permits description: null to clear the optional description; keep name non-null.

docs.title: Staff
docs.text:
A staff member belongs to a hospital, can have multiple roles, and can be assigned patients. Defined in app/models/staff.py; managed through /staff.

Field Type Required on create Validation id integer Generated Primary key first_name string Yes 1–100 characters last_name string Yes 1–100 characters hospital_id integer Yes Existing hospital checked on create role_ids integer array No Defaults to []; referenced roles must exist

role_ids is a create/update/read schema field, not a column in staff. The ORM stores relationships through staff_roles. Read responses return sorted role IDs. There is no singular role field.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "first_name":"Olivia",
  "last_name":"Chen",
  "hospital_id":1,
  "role_ids":[1,2]
}

docs.title: Role updates
docs.text: PATCH with role_ids: [1,2] replaces current roles. role_ids: [] clears them. Omitting the field or setting it to null leaves roles unchanged. Duplicate IDs are deduplicated through the relationship query. Invalid role references return 400.

docs.title: Relationship limitations
docs.text: Creating a staff member validates its hospital. Updating a hospital without also updating roles does not use the same reference-validation helper, and moving staff does not revalidate assigned patients. Keep patient assignments consistent before moves. Delete dependent patients before staff, or explicitly unassign patients through patient PATCH. Required staff fields must remain non-null.
